transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what finally got me to make an appointment is that my concentration has gotten really unreliable lately. I'll be at the clinic reviewing a patient's chart, or even just at home laying out a watercolor wash, and suddenly I realize I’ve read the same line three times. My mind just keeps wandering off to everything that could possibly go wrong.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty concentrating and this excessive worrying—days, weeks, or months?
Well, definitely months. It's actually been going on since I started the formal retirement process at the practice... so that would be about a year and three months ago, I'd say.
Over these past several months, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your watercolor painting?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. I still enjoy painting and things like that, it's just... hard to focus on them sometimes because my mind is always racing with worries. But the interest is definitely still there.

Would you say your worrying is mostly about your retirement and what comes next, or do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things in your life—like your health, finances, family, or other everyday matters?

It's really about a lot of different things. My mind just keeps circling around all sorts of issues. I worry about whether my old patients are being looked after properly by the new staff. I stress over whether the financial side of the practice handoff is completely sound. And then I worry about myself, you know, whether I'll just become useless once I'm fully retired. It's not just one thing, and honestly, the amount of worrying I do feels completely out of proportion even to me.
Along with the worrying, have you noticed physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling restless or on edge, tiring easily, or trouble sleeping?

Well, the sleeping part is definitely an issue. Most nights, I get into bed feeling pretty tired, but... as soon as the house gets quiet, my mind just turns on. I start replaying patient transfers and all the money details. And even when I do finally get to sleep, I end up waking up at four or five in the morning, feeling like I never really settled down.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with chronic (>1 year) excessive, uncontrollable worry about multiple domains (patient care, finances, self-worth) that is disproportionate to actual circumstances, accompanied by concentration difficulties and sleep disturbance (initial and early-morning awakening). Mood is euthymic with preserved interest and pleasure in activities (e.g., painting), ruling out a depressive episode. Although onset coincided with retirement (a psychosocial stressor), the worry has generalized beyond the stressor itself to multiple unrelated areas and has persisted well beyond expected adjustment timelines, making Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) the best fit rather than Adjustment Disorder.

Denies loss of interest or pleasure in activities (still enjoys painting)
